newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in Barclays.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in Barclays.

text.p: Traded options in Barclays Bank were active as the underlying stock raced up on Wednesday, dealers said.

The main deals were from traders taking a view on the future volatility of the stock by trading strangles. One of the largest deals by mid-afternoon was from a buyer of 300 April 1150 calls at 34p as well as 300 April 1100 puts at 36p.
In contrast, and in a separate deal, there was a seller of these strangles at the same prices.
For a profit at expiry the holder of the long strangles needs Barclays' shares to either go below 1030p or above 1220p.
The seller of the strangles requires Barclays' shares to stay within 1100p and 1150p at expiry.
By 1448 GMT, the underlying shares had notched up 13p to 1122-1/2p and the bank will announce its annual results on February 18.
Over in bio-science group Zeneca a bull spread was bought. It consisted of buying 300 April 1700 calls at 70p and selling 300 April 1800 calls at 35p making a net debit of 35p.
A maximum profit of 65p will be made at expiry if Zeneca shares go above 1800p. A maximum loss of 35p will be realised if the shares stay below 1700p. Breakeven is at 1735p.
Zeneca shares jumped up 29p to 1671-1/2p as unconfirmed rumours of a merger with Swiss drugs company Roche circulated in the market.
Elsewhere, there was a buyer of 1,000 March 2420 calls at 7p in British Gas whose shares were unchanged 227-1/2p.
And in insurance group Prudential Corporation in two separate deals 500 May 550 puts were bought at 45p and 46p each as the shares tumbled 13p to 524p.
There was also a buyer of 500 March 140 puts in Lonrho. The shares were unchanged at 129p.
